[SPARK-BRIEF.md#BBB3]
1:# Etched in Schema — brief for Muse Spark
2:
3:Hackathon: Meta Model API, **Startup Track — judged on a working product**.
4:Builder: Jeremy Hobson (3tched).
5:
6:**Scope (owner, 2026-10-28):** the identity/3tched platform predates the
7:hackathon and is used through its interfaces. The new, judged development is
8:(1) compliance routing, (2) rule enforcement, (3) policy, and (4) a drop-in
9:consumer app (team chat first). The UI is optional. See README "Goals" for the
10:golden path. Sections below about the avatar, CMS demo and on-chain anchoring
11:are background, not the critical path.
12:State as of 2026-10-28. Everything marked **proven** was demonstrated on the
13:host that day; everything else is planned.
14:
15:## The project in one paragraph
16:
17:A self-contained 3tched identity — the "twin", the living embodiment of a
18:3tched subsidiary — turns a business goal into deployed, verified
19:infrastructure. It acts only through its own typed filesystem (3tchedFS),
20:every action is authorised against its capabilities and leaves a
21:tamper-evident receipt, and a Web3 index anchored on-chain lets anyone verify
22:who did what, under what authority, without trusting the agent or operator.
23:That link between on-chain artifacts and accountable, authorised actors is the
24:gap blocking Web3 adoption.
25:
26:## Proven today
27:
28:- **Identity container**: `3tchedCtlChatbot` (Incus, pool `3tched`, profile
29:  `3tched-lungs`), identity session `b0c777e3-0955-cd8b-3d01-ca12998cae28`,
30:  service principal, persist volume, kept running by runit `chatbot-identity`.
31:- **First-person operation call**: inside the container, write the plain JSON
32:  arguments to `/run/mount/3tchedfs/operations/<plugin>/<method>/call` (open
33:  read-write, write, fsync, read back on the same handle). Example
34:  `identity_sled/get_own_identity` with `{}` returned the identity, operation
35:  `51c8f91c-c2f1-4688-a985-fb41684adfff`, chain events 10389/10390, outcome
36:  completed. The bridge identifies the caller from the kernel peer over the
37:  lungs Unix socket, checks the exact capability, commits via MutationEngine.
38:- **Infrastructure operations available to the identity**: `incus/*`
39:  (create/start/stop/snapshot/devices), `ovsdb_bridge/*` (bridges, ports,
40:  transact), plus ~70 plugins. Each call is checked against the identity's
41:  grants.
42:- **No network path to 3tched**: the twin talks to 3tched only through its FUSE
43:  mount. Its only network will be the internet (Meta API, blockchain).
44:- **Chat path**: UI (`http://10.0.0.2:8080`) → door `10.0.0.2:8090` →
45:  `chat_router.Chat` → zeroclaw router on `127.0.0.1:8084` (protocol
46:  `zeroclaw.v1`) → model. Every turn receipted.
47:- **Avatar**: `IdentityAvatar.svelte` speaks a fixed intro script (exact
48:  wording, no model) and answers spoken or typed questions via the chat path.
49:
50:## Where things are
51:
52:| Thing | Path |
53:|---|---|
54:| Backend (Rust workspace) | `/srv/git/odbus-verified` — read its `AGENTS.md` and `HANDOFF.md` first |
55:| UI (SvelteKit + json-render) | `/srv/git/3tched.com` (has uncommitted WIP — do not publish it as-is) |
56:| UI build actually live | scratch worktree of 3tched.com HEAD + `tched_router`→`chat_router` + avatar |
57:| This repo | `/srv/git/etched-in-schema` — Web3 index schema, LLC declaration schema |
58:| Recovered execution tracker | branch `recover/execution-tracker`, worktree `/srv/git/odbus-tracker-recover` (compiles; not deployed) |
59:| Router config | `/var/lib/tched-router/config.toml` (root; backups `*.bak-20261028-*`) |
60:| Qdrant | `127.0.0.1:6333` — `repos_specs_docs_voyage_4_lite`, `repos_repomix_voyage_context_4`, `snowball_footprints`, `blockchain_footprints` |
61:
62:## Rules that must not be broken
63:
64:- The plugin IS the schema. Backend schemas live only in Rust plugins under
65:  `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/`, sealed into blobs. No standalone
66:  schema files in op-dbus (that is why drafts live in this repo).
67:- UI is Svelte/SvelteKit + Vite + json-render's Svelte renderer only. Every
68:  visible element is a catalog component.
69:- Never edit Cozo directly, never bypass a permission denial, never add or
70:  remove Btrfs members outside explicit identity provisioning.
71:- Deployment is `./activate-golden.sh` / `op-release-launch release`
72:  (btrfs send/receive slots). Never hand-copy binaries onto the host as a deploy.
73:- One Cargo process at a time; release builds need `CXXFLAGS="-include cstdint"`.
74:- Tests only when the owner asks.
75:
76:## Plan (10 days)
77:
78:1. OSCAL catalog of 3tched capabilities with a tag taxonomy; component
79:   definitions for 3–5 plugins (Compliance Trestle is installed: `trestle`).
80:2. Tag routing: profile → components → plugin operations.
81:3. Boundary rules compiled into capability grants and budgets (the bridge
82:   already enforces grants on every call).
83:4. "Create a CMS for this business": business declaration (start with
84:   `schema/llc-declaration.schema.json`) → profile → provision via the twin,
85:   receipts recorded as OSCAL assessment results and anchored on-chain.
86:5. UI: avatar intro, then "enough about me — here's what I can do for your
87:   business" (scripted once the business is chosen), vitals and nerve-trace
88:   views fed by real receipts, OSCAL views.
89:Golden path (must work three times in a row before any stretch goal):
90:scripted intro → "create a CMS for this business" from one small declaration
91:and one OSCAL profile → the twin provisions one or two real things through its
92:own mount, with a visible nerve trace and receipts → one receipt anchored
93:on-chain → a judge verifies it themselves.
94:
95:Out of scope (owner, 2026-10-28): moving the identity between hosts
96:("astral projection") — no business case. Client acquisition is optional; add
97:it only if it fits the flow.
98:
99:## Known open issues
100:
101:- Meta model not yet wired into the router (no Meta API key on the host;
102:  Junie reaches Muse Spark through its JetBrains login). Hermes has a `Meta`
103:  custom provider stub (`HERMES_CUSTOM_META_API_KEY`).
104:- Router turn costs ~15k tokens (skills bundle removed to halve it). Qwen does
105:  not reliably emit text tool calls; MCP compact tools are connected
106:  (`https://10.0.0.2:8090/mcp`) but retrieval answers came back empty.
107:- Live state reads through the mount (`plugins/*/value.json`) return EIO.
108:- Next release will fail activation: `notebook-sources-sync` cannot pass its
109:  30 s check after restart. Fix before releasing.
110:- Re-key of the core chatbot to the WireGuard server key (session
111:  `58287215-0136-f7c3-0a02-d51a593b75ef`) has no supported op yet.
112:- UI overlay on `dashboard-release` is runtime-only; lost on reboot or release.
113:
114:## CMS: compliant by construction (owner direction, 2026-10-28)
115:
116:The CMS is the showcase because it comes out usable *and* evidently
117:controlled. Pick a handful of controls whose effect is visible on stage; each
118:control → a CMS behaviour → evidence (receipt or anchor):
119:
120:| Control area | Visible behaviour | Evidence |
121:|---|---|---|
122:| PII handling (NIST 800-53 PT) | automatic redaction on publish; original kept only in the owner's private scope | redaction operation receipt naming the triggering policy |
123:| Audit (AU) | every create/edit/publish attributable | receipt chain: who, capability, when |
124:| Access control (AC) | roles compiled into capability grants | a live denial showing the exact missing capability |
125:| Retention (SI-12) | scheduled expiry/archive | scheduled operation receipt |
126:| Integrity | published versions hash-anchored | on-chain anchor a judge can check |
127:
128:Pitch wording: "implements and evidences these controls" — never "compliant"
129:or "certified" (an assessor declares compliance).
130:
131:## Remote identities: established design (owner, 2026-10-28)
132:
133:WireGuard is only the establishment step: the peer key proves the identity
134:once, the decoy issues the signed peer proof (OIA1) and the session gets its
135:sealed credential (SID1). After that it is zero trust — every call carries the
136:credential and the door's interceptor re-verifies it, over any transport
137:(internet, Cloudflare). 3tched-fs `Credential` mode is the remote form of the
138:lungs. The mechanism exists; it needs testing and refinement, not a rebuild.
139:Do not add a mesh (Netmaker/Cloudflare) as an identity layer.
140:
141:## Progress log
142:
143:- 2026-10-28: Junie pinned to Muse Spark for this repo — new
144:  `.junie/config.json` sets `model: muse-spark-1.3`, `effort: medium`
145:  (matches `~/.junie/settings.json` launch default, provider `meta`).
146:  IDE Junie routes via JetBrains login, no key needed. Headless `junie --task`
147:  still unauthenticated ("Cannot find authorization", proven this date):
148:  needs `JUNIE_META_API_KEY` from `https://ai.developer.meta.com/`
149:  (documented in `docs/RUNTIME.md`); same key gap blocks runtime Meta calls
150:  for the drop-in.
151:- 2026-10-28: LiteLLM wired to Meta Model API — `META_API_KEY` (48ch),
152:  `META_MODEL=muse-spark-1.3`, `META_MODEL_BASE_URL=https://api.meta.ai/v1`
153:  present in `~/.bash_secrets` and `/home/3tched/.config/etched/env` (0600).
154:  Venv `~/.venvs/litellm-meta` (litellm lib) proven: `openai/muse-spark-1.3`
155:  + api_base override returns `litellm-meta-ok` (~7s, 204 reasoning tokens).
156:  Helper `tools/litellm_meta.py` uses only `META_*` env, `max_tokens=800`
157:  default. Note: SPARK-BRIEF line 148 `JUNIE_META_API_KEY` gap is separate
158:  (headless Junie auth); runtime Meta calls are unblocked.
159:- 2026-10-28: omp in this repo is meta+jev only — new `.omp/config.yml`
160:  (project scope, other dirs unaffected): `disabledProviders` denies all 22
161:  non-meta chat providers (proven: `omp models` here lists 1 provider,
162:  `openai`/`salad` gone; /tmp still lists 23, smol still global salad).
163:  `modelRoles` pins default/smol/slow/plan/advisor to meta, judge stays
164:  `typesafe/jev-latest`; all `task.agentModelOverrides` mapped to meta.
165:  `enabledProviders` allowlist does NOT work at project scope (tested).
166:  Shell env fixed for consistency: `~/.bashrc` now sources
167:  `~/.bash_secrets` first; `~/.profile` stale `/home/admin/.bash_secrets`
168:  path repointed to `$HOME`. Clean-env `omp -p --model meta/muse-spark-1.3`
169:  returns `omp-meta-ok` (~7s). Broker cred hash == `META_API_KEY` hash.

# Etched in Schema — brief for Muse Spark

Hackathon: Meta Model API, **Startup Track — judged on a working product**.
Builder: Jeremy Hobson (3tched).

**Scope (owner, 2026-10-28):** the identity/3tched platform predates the
hackathon and is used through its interfaces. The new, judged development is
(1) compliance routing, (2) rule enforcement, (3) policy, and (4) a drop-in
consumer app (team chat first). The UI is optional. See README "Goals" for the
golden path. Sections below about the avatar, CMS demo and on-chain anchoring
are background, not the critical path.
State as of 2026-10-28. Everything marked **proven** was demonstrated on the
host that day; everything else is planned.

## The project in one paragraph

A self-contained 3tched identity — the "twin", the living embodiment of a
3tched subsidiary — turns a business goal into deployed, verified
infrastructure. It acts only through its own typed filesystem (3tchedFS),
every action is authorised against its capabilities and leaves a
tamper-evident receipt, and a Web3 index anchored on-chain lets anyone verify
who did what, under what authority, without trusting the agent or operator.
That link between on-chain artifacts and accountable, authorised actors is the
gap blocking Web3 adoption.

## Proven today

- **Identity container**: `3tchedCtlChatbot` (Incus, pool `3tched`, profile
  `3tched-lungs`), identity session `b0c777e3-0955-cd8b-3d01-ca12998cae28`,
  service principal, persist volume, kept running by runit `chatbot-identity`.
- **First-person operation call**: inside the container, write the plain JSON
  arguments to `/run/mount/3tchedfs/operations/<plugin>/<method>/call` (open
  read-write, write, fsync, read back on the same handle). Example
  `identity_sled/get_own_identity` with `{}` returned the identity, operation
  `51c8f91c-c2f1-4688-a985-fb41684adfff`, chain events 10389/10390, outcome
  completed. The bridge identifies the caller from the kernel peer over the
  lungs Unix socket, checks the exact capability, commits via MutationEngine.
- **Infrastructure operations available to the identity**: `incus/*`
  (create/start/stop/snapshot/devices), `ovsdb_bridge/*` (bridges, ports,
  transact), plus ~70 plugins. Each call is checked against the identity's
  grants.
- **No network path to 3tched**: the twin talks to 3tched only through its FUSE
  mount. Its only network will be the internet (Meta API, blockchain).
- **Chat path**: UI (`http://10.0.0.2:8080`) → door `10.0.0.2:8090` →
  `chat_router.Chat` → zeroclaw router on `127.0.0.1:8084` (protocol
  `zeroclaw.v1`) → model. Every turn receipted.
- **Avatar**: `IdentityAvatar.svelte` speaks a fixed intro script (exact
  wording, no model) and answers spoken or typed questions via the chat path.

## Where things are

| Thing | Path |
|---|---|
| Backend (Rust workspace) | `/srv/git/odbus-verified` — read its `AGENTS.md` and `HANDOFF.md` first |
| UI (SvelteKit + json-render) | `/srv/git/3tched.com` (has uncommitted WIP — do not publish it as-is) |
| UI build actually live | scratch worktree of 3tched.com HEAD + `tched_router`→`chat_router` + avatar |
| This repo | `/srv/git/etched-in-schema` — Web3 index schema, LLC declaration schema |
| Recovered execution tracker | branch `recover/execution-tracker`, worktree `/srv/git/odbus-tracker-recover` (compiles; not deployed) |
| Router config | `/var/lib/tched-router/config.toml` (root; backups `*.bak-20261028-*`) |
| Qdrant | `127.0.0.1:6333` — `repos_specs_docs_voyage_4_lite`, `repos_repomix_voyage_context_4`, `snowball_footprints`, `blockchain_footprints` |

## Rules that must not be broken

- The plugin IS the schema. Backend schemas live only in Rust plugins under
  `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/`, sealed into blobs. No standalone
  schema files in op-dbus (that is why drafts live in this repo).
- UI is Svelte/SvelteKit + Vite + json-render's Svelte renderer only. Every
  visible element is a catalog component.
- Never edit Cozo directly, never bypass a permission denial, never add or
  remove Btrfs members outside explicit identity provisioning.
- Deployment is `./activate-golden.sh` / `op-release-launch release`
  (btrfs send/receive slots). Never hand-copy binaries onto the host as a deploy.
- One Cargo process at a time; release builds need `CXXFLAGS="-include cstdint"`.
- Tests only when the owner asks.

## Plan (10 days)

1. OSCAL catalog of 3tched capabilities with a tag taxonomy; component
   definitions for 3–5 plugins (Compliance Trestle is installed: `trestle`).
2. Tag routing: profile → components → plugin operations.
3. Boundary rules compiled into capability grants and budgets (the bridge
   already enforces grants on every call).
4. "Create a CMS for this business": business declaration (start with
   `schema/llc-declaration.schema.json`) → profile → provision via the twin,
   receipts recorded as OSCAL assessment results and anchored on-chain.
5. UI: avatar intro, then "enough about me — here's what I can do for your
   business" (scripted once the business is chosen), vitals and nerve-trace
   views fed by real receipts, OSCAL views.
Golden path (must work three times in a row before any stretch goal):
scripted intro → "create a CMS for this business" from one small declaration
and one OSCAL profile → the twin provisions one or two real things through its
own mount, with a visible nerve trace and receipts → one receipt anchored
on-chain → a judge verifies it themselves.

Out of scope (owner, 2026-10-28): moving the identity between hosts
("astral projection") — no business case. Client acquisition is optional; add
it only if it fits the flow.

## Known open issues

- Meta model not yet wired into the router (no Meta API key on the host;
  Junie reaches Muse Spark through its JetBrains login). Hermes has a `Meta`
  custom provider stub (`HERMES_CUSTOM_META_API_KEY`).
- Router turn costs ~15k tokens (skills bundle removed to halve it). Qwen does
  not reliably emit text tool calls; MCP compact tools are connected
  (`https://10.0.0.2:8090/mcp`) but retrieval answers came back empty.
- Live state reads through the mount (`plugins/*/value.json`) return EIO.
- Next release will fail activation: `notebook-sources-sync` cannot pass its
  30 s check after restart. Fix before releasing.
- Re-key of the core chatbot to the WireGuard server key (session
  `58287215-0136-f7c3-0a02-d51a593b75ef`) has no supported op yet.
- UI overlay on `dashboard-release` is runtime-only; lost on reboot or release.

## CMS: compliant by construction (owner direction, 2026-10-28)

The CMS is the showcase because it comes out usable *and* evidently
controlled. Pick a handful of controls whose effect is visible on stage; each
control → a CMS behaviour → evidence (receipt or anchor):

| Control area | Visible behaviour | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| PII handling (NIST 800-53 PT) | automatic redaction on publish; original kept only in the owner's private scope | redaction operation receipt naming the triggering policy |
| Audit (AU) | every create/edit/publish attributable | receipt chain: who, capability, when |
| Access control (AC) | roles compiled into capability grants | a live denial showing the exact missing capability |
| Retention (SI-12) | scheduled expiry/archive | scheduled operation receipt |
| Integrity | published versions hash-anchored | on-chain anchor a judge can check |

Pitch wording: "implements and evidences these controls" — never "compliant"
or "certified" (an assessor declares compliance).

## Remote identities: established design (owner, 2026-10-28)

WireGuard is only the establishment step: the peer key proves the identity
once, the decoy issues the signed peer proof (OIA1) and the session gets its
sealed credential (SID1). After that it is zero trust — every call carries the
credential and the door's interceptor re-verifies it, over any transport
(internet, Cloudflare). 3tched-fs `Credential` mode is the remote form of the
lungs. The mechanism exists; it needs testing and refinement, not a rebuild.
Do not add a mesh (Netmaker/Cloudflare) as an identity layer.

## Progress log

- 2026-10-28: Junie pinned to Muse Spark for this repo — new
  `.junie/config.json` sets `model: muse-spark-1.3`, `effort: medium`
  (matches `~/.junie/settings.json` launch default, provider `meta`).
  IDE Junie routes via JetBrains login, no key needed. Headless `junie --task`

  needs `JUNIE_META_API_KEY` from `https://ai.developer.meta.com/`
  (documented in `docs/RUNTIME.md`); same key gap blocks runtime Meta calls
  for the drop-in.

  `META_MODEL=muse-spark-1.3`, `META_MODEL_BASE_URL=https://api.meta.ai/v1`
  present in `~/.bash_secrets` and `/home/3tched/.config/etched/env` (0600).
  Venv `~/.venvs/litellm-meta` (litellm lib) proven: `openai/muse-spark-1.3`
  + api_base override returns `litellm-meta-ok` (~7s, 204 reasoning tokens).
  Helper `tools/litellm_meta.py` uses only `META_*` env, `max_tokens=800`
  default. Note: SPARK-BRIEF line 148 `JUNIE_META_API_KEY` gap is separate
  (headless Junie auth); runtime Meta calls are unblocked.
- 2026-10-28: omp in this repo is meta+jev only — new `.omp/config.yml`
  (project scope, other dirs unaffected): `disabledProviders` denies all 22
  non-meta chat providers (proven: `omp models` here lists 1 provider,
  `openai`/`salad` gone; /tmp still lists 23, smol still global salad).
  `modelRoles` pins default/smol/slow/plan/advisor to meta, judge stays
  `typesafe/jev-latest`; all `task.agentModelOverrides` mapped to meta.

18:6. `docs/SUBSIDIARY-SLED.md` — identity, root, subsidiaries, approvals

73:
74:# Etched in Schema
75:
76:**An identity that acts — and can prove what it did.**
77:
78:Etched in Schema is a self-contained 3tched identity — the living embodiment
79:of a business subsidiary — that turns a business goal into deployed,
80:working infrastructure. Every action it takes is authorised against its
81:capabilities, bounded by compliance rules, recorded as a tamper-evident
82:receipt, and anchored on a blockchain so anyone can verify *who did what,
83:under what authority, and what actually happened* without trusting the agent
84:or its operator.
85:
86:Built for the Meta Model API hackathon (Startup Track — judged on a working
87:product) by Jeremy Hobson, founder of 3tched.
88:
89:## Why
90:
91:AI agents can reason about goals, but they rarely have a durable identity,
92:verifiable permissions, accountable execution, or the ability to build and
93:operate real systems. On-chain artifacts have the mirror-image problem: a
94:contract address or a content hash proves something exists, not that it came
95:from an accountable actor following permitted steps. That missing link
96:between artifacts and accountable, authorised actors is what keeps businesses
97:from trusting both autonomous agents and Web3.
98:
99:Etched in Schema closes that gap from both sides: every on-chain artifact
100:points to the identity and authorised operation behind it, and every
101:operation points to the artifacts it produced, with the history anchored
102:on-chain.
103:
104:## Goals — the new, judged product
105:
106:The identity platform (3tched) existed before the hackathon and is used only
107:through its interfaces. The **new development, built and judged here**, is:
108:
109:1. **Compliance routing** — a business's requirements become an OSCAL profile;
110:   OSCAL tags route each request and each requirement to the components and
111:   plugin operations that implement it.
112:2. **Rule enforcement** — boundary rules compile into the capability grants,
113:   budgets and network policy that are enforced on every call, with a clear
114:   refusal (and the exact missing capability) when a request is out of bounds.
115:3. **Policy** — authoring, versioning and evaluating the rules: what each
116:   identity may do, which actions need human approval (two approvals for root),
117:   and what happens to data (e.g. PII redaction, retention).
118:4. **Drop-in consumer app** — the existing UI generator repurposed: one spec
119:   renders on the web and in tools people already use, starting with **team chat** — an open-source
120:   Matrix client (Element) first, reaching other chat tools through Matrix
121:   bridges — and every action is governed by 1–3. Spec:
122:   [docs/DROP-IN-SPEC.md](docs/DROP-IN-SPEC.md).
123:   A user asks in team chat; the request is routed, checked against policy,
124:   executed through the identity or refused, and the receipt comes back in the
125:   thread.
126:
127:The web UI is optional, only if time allows.
128:
129:**Golden path** (a working product, end to end, three times in a row before
130:anything else): a user asks the agent in team chat to do something for a business
131:→ compliance routing maps it to the required controls and operations →
132:policy is evaluated → allowed operations run through the identity and return
133:receipts; a disallowed one is refused with the reason → the thread shows the
134:result, the receipts, and any redaction applied.
135:
136:Out of the critical path: the avatar/embodiment, moving identities between
137:hosts, client acquisition, and on-chain anchoring (kept only if it fits once
138:the golden path works).
139:
140:## What is new vs. what already exists
141:
142:Everything in **this repository** is developed during the hackathon. It is
143:built *on* 3tched, which already exists and is used only through its
144:published interfaces (see [docs/3TCHED-RESOURCES.md](docs/3TCHED-RESOURCES.md)).
145:
146:| New in this repo (judged) | Existing 3tched resource it uses |
147:|---|---|
148:| OSCAL catalog of 3tched capabilities, tag taxonomy, profiles, component definitions | `oscal_subid_registry` (subid discovery), `schema_tag_registry` (tag metadata, owner-scoped policy) |
149:| Compliance router: request / profile → controls → plugin operations | sealed plugin catalog, identity operation files (3tchedFS) |
150:| Rule enforcement: OSCAL rules → capability grants, budgets, OpenFlow policy; refusals with reasons | bridge per-call capability check, `openflow` / `ovsdb_bridge`, router budgets |
151:| Policy engine and policy documents (approvals, redaction, retention) | `schema_tag_registry` policies, `routing_decision`, `elevation` |
152:| Drop-in consumer app: team chat first (Matrix/Element) | chat path to Meta's model, identity receipts |
153:| Business declarations (starting with a Florida LLC) | — |
154:
155:Pre-existing and **not** part of the judged work: the identity container and
156:sled, kernel-peer admission, 3tchedFS, the bridge and MutationEngine, receipts,
157:the router, and the 3tched.com UI.
158:
159:## Architecture at a glance
160:
161:```
162:          internet only                      local filesystem only
163:  Meta model API  ◄──┐                 ┌──► 3tchedFS mount (lungs) ──► 3tched bridge
164:  blockchain      ◄──┤   IDENTITY      │      kernel-peer identity, capability check,
165:                     └── CONTAINER  ───┘      MutationEngine commit, receipt
166:                          (the twin)
167:                               │
168:            OSCAL profile ─► tag router ─► plugin operations (incus, openflow, …)
169:                               │
170:                  receipts ─► Web3 index ─► Merkle root anchored on-chain
171:```
172:
173:- The identity has **no network path to 3tched**; it reaches 3tched only
174:  through its own FUSE mount, where every operation is a typed file.
175:- Its only network is the internet: the Meta model API and the blockchain.
176:- Subsidiaries map to Linux users; the root is the 3tched control plane.
177:  See [docs/SUBSIDIARY-SLED.md](docs/SUBSIDIARY-SLED.md).
178:- How this compares to SPIFFE, BeyondCorp and DIDs, and what it adds:
179:  [docs/PRIOR-ART.md](docs/PRIOR-ART.md).

182:
183:| Path | Contents |
184:|---|---|
185:| `schema/` | JSON Schemas: Web3 index entry, business declarations |
186:| `oscal/` | OSCAL catalog, profiles, component definitions (Compliance Trestle workspace) |
187:| `routing/` | tag router: profile → components → operations |
188:| `enforcement/` | boundary compiler: OSCAL rules → grants, budgets, OpenFlow policy |
189:| `consumer/` | drop-in consumer apps (team chat first) |
190:| `cms/` | the CMS and its control behaviours (background) |
191:| `web3/` | index log, Merkle anchoring |
192:| `ui/` | Svelte components for the 3tched.com app |
193:| `START-HERE.md`, `CONTEXT.md` | open in Junie; CONTEXT.md bundles every doc (rebuild with `tools/build-context.sh`) |
194:| `docs/` | 3tched resources, subsidiary/sled model, prior art and positioning, how to win |
195:| `SPARK-BRIEF.md` | current state, rules, open issues, progress log |
196:
197:## Working rules
198:
199:- Read `SPARK-BRIEF.md` before starting; log progress at its end (dated).
200:- Mark claims as **proven** (demonstrated, with evidence) or **planned**.
201:- Schemas here are drafts; promoted ones become sealed 3tched plugins (Rust).
202:- UI: Svelte/SvelteKit + json-render's Svelte renderer only.
203:- In pitches say "implements and evidences these controls", never
204:  "compliant" or "certified".
205:
206:---
207:
208:## FILE: `docs/DROP-IN-SPEC.md`
209:
210:# Drop-in spec: one generator, every surface
211:
212:The drop-in is the existing 3tched UI generator, repurposed: the same spec
213:pipeline that renders the web UI also renders into consumer apps (team chat
214:first), and every action it exposes is governed by the new compliance
215:routing, policy and enforcement.
216:
217:Marked **existing** (3tched today, used through its interfaces) or **new**
218:(built and judged in this repository).
219:
220:## 1. What the generator does today (existing)
221:
222:| Capability | Where it lives |
223:|---|---|
224:| **Catalog**: the components a UI may use, as sealed declarations (Canvas profile, whole-application contract, imported shadcn component schemas) | `json_render` plugin: `list_catalog`, `list_components`, `get_component_schema`, `get_catalog_entry` |
225:| **Spec**: a json-render element tree, validated against the catalog | `json_render`: `get_spec_schema`, `validate_spec`, `export_json_schema` |
226:| **Generation**: the model is given the catalog surface and writes a spec; the spec is validated before rendering | `json_render`: `build_prompt_surface`; chat application mode (`json_render_generation`) |
227:| **Deterministic rendering**: a UI built directly from a plugin's sealed schema, no model involved | `schema_renderer`: `render_schema`, `get_rendering`, `validate_schema`, `list_galleries` |
228:| **Gallery**: specs a human kept, saved as candidates and promoted into catalog entries | `json_render`: `save_candidate`, `list_candidates`, `promote_candidate`, `retire_catalog_entry` |
229:| **Actions and events**: elements bound to plugin operations; events handled and components updated | `json_render`: `list_actions`; `web_ui`: `render_page`, `handle_event`, `update_component` |
230:| **Renderers** | `json_render`: `list_renderers`, `list_packages`; web renderer: json-render's Svelte renderer in 3tched.com |
231:
232:Rules that carry over unchanged: every visible element is declared in the
233:catalog; specs are validated before they are shown; the plugin is the schema.
234:
235:**The generator is proven** (owner, 2026-10-28): it did this job well before
236:any compliance layer existed. Reuse it as is. Do not rebuild generation,
237:validation or the catalog; the new work is only the team chat renderer target, the
238:five governance components (2.3), and routing every action through
239:compliance, policy and enforcement (2.2).
240:
241:## 2. What the drop-in adds (new)
242:
243:### 2.1 Renderer targets
244:
245:One spec, several targets. A target renders the catalog components it
246:supports and degrades the rest predictably (never drops an action or a
247:refusal silently).
248:
249:| Target | Status | Notes |
250:|---|---|---|
251:| Web (Svelte) | existing | reference renderer |
252:| **team chat** (Matrix message) | new — first | messages, modals, interactive buttons |
253:| Teams (Adaptive Cards), email (HTML) | new — later | same mapping approach |
254:
255:Component → team chat mapping (initial):
256:
257:| Catalog component | Matrix messages (HTML + reactions/buttons via widgets) |
258:|---|---|
259:| heading, text | `header`, `section` (mrkdwn) |
260:| key/value facts | `section` with `fields` |
261:| list, table (small) | `section` lines; large tables → attached file + summary |
262:| button / action | `actions` with `button` (value = action id) |
263:| select, input | modal with `static_select` / `plain_text_input` |
264:| status / progress | `context` line with state |
265:| **receipt** (new) | `context`: operation id, outcome, capability, event hash |
266:| **refusal** (new) | `section` with the exact missing capability and the rule that refused |
267:| **approval request** (new) | `actions` Approve / Reject, shows approvals so far (e.g. 1 of 2) |
268:| **redaction notice** (new) | `context`: what was redacted and which policy did it |
269:
270:### 2.2 Governed actions
271:
272:Every action, on every target, takes one path:
273:
274:```
275:user action (web click / team chat button / team chat command)
276:  → consumer adapter (identifies the user; no authority of its own)
277:  → compliance router: request → OSCAL controls → candidate plugin operations
278:  → policy engine: allow / refuse (with reason) / needs approval (n of m)
279:  → enforcement: the operation runs through the identity's 3tchedFS call file;
280:    the bridge checks the exact capability and commits
281:  → result + receipt rendered back on the same target
282:```
283:
284:- The adapter never calls plugins directly and never holds grants.
285:- A refusal is a first-class result, rendered with the missing capability and
286:  the rule.
287:- Approvals are collected on the target (chat buttons) and counted by the
288:  policy engine; root actions need two different humans.
289:- Redaction is applied by policy before content reaches any target; the
290:  receipt records it.
291:
292:### 2.3 New catalog components
293:
294:`receipt`, `refusal`, `approval_request`, `redaction_notice`, `policy_decision`.
295:They are declared in the catalog like every other component (web and team chat
296:renderers both implement them).
297:
298:### 2.4 Generation stays the same
299:
300:The model (Meta's) still writes specs from the catalog surface; the spec is
…
302:model to components the destination supports.

   executed through the identity or refused, and the receipt comes back in the
   thread.

The web UI is optional, only if time allows.

**Golden path** (a working product, end to end, three times in a row before
anything else): a user asks the agent in team chat to do something for a business
→ compliance routing maps it to the required controls and operations →
policy is evaluated → allowed operations run through the identity and return
receipts; a disallowed one is refused with the reason → the thread shows the
result, the receipts, and any redaction applied.

Out of the critical path: the avatar/embodiment, moving identities between
hosts, client acquisition, and on-chain anchoring (kept only if it fits once
the golden path works).

## What is new vs. what already exists

Everything in **this repository** is developed during the hackathon. It is
built *on* 3tched, which already exists and is used only through its
published interfaces (see [docs/3TCHED-RESOURCES.md](docs/3TCHED-RESOURCES.md)).

| New in this repo (judged) | Existing 3tched resource it uses |
|---|---|
| OSCAL catalog of 3tched capabilities, tag taxonomy, profiles, component definitions | `oscal_subid_registry` (subid discovery), `schema_tag_registry` (tag metadata, owner-scoped policy) |
| Compliance router: request / profile → controls → plugin operations | sealed plugin catalog, identity operation files (3tchedFS) |
| Rule enforcement: OSCAL rules → capability grants, budgets, OpenFlow policy; refusals with reasons | bridge per-call capability check, `openflow` / `ovsdb_bridge`, router budgets |
| Policy engine and policy documents (approvals, redaction, retention) | `schema_tag_registry` policies, `routing_decision`, `elevation` |
| Drop-in consumer app: team chat first (Matrix/Element) | chat path to Meta's model, identity receipts |
| Business declarations (starting with a Florida LLC) | — |

Pre-existing and **not** part of the judged work: the identity container and
sled, kernel-peer admission, 3tchedFS, the bridge and MutationEngine, receipts,
the router, and the 3tched.com UI.

## Architecture at a glance

```
          internet only                      local filesystem only
  Meta model API  ◄──┐                 ┌──► 3tchedFS mount (lungs) ──► 3tched bridge
  blockchain      ◄──┤   IDENTITY      │      kernel-peer identity, capability check,
                     └── CONTAINER  ───┘      MutationEngine commit, receipt
                          (the twin)
                               │
            OSCAL profile ─► tag router ─► plugin operations (incus, openflow, …)
                               │
                  receipts ─► Web3 index ─► Merkle root anchored on-chain
```

- The identity has **no network path to 3tched**; it reaches 3tched only
  through its own FUSE mount, where every operation is a typed file.
- Its only network is the internet: the Meta model API and the blockchain.
- Subsidiaries map to Linux users; the root is the 3tched control plane.
  See [docs/SUBSIDIARY-SLED.md](docs/SUBSIDIARY-SLED.md).
- How this compares to SPIFFE, BeyondCorp and DIDs, and what it adds:
  [docs/PRIOR-ART.md](docs/PRIOR-ART.md).

## Repository layout

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `schema/` | JSON Schemas: Web3 index entry, business declarations |
| `oscal/` | OSCAL catalog, profiles, component definitions (Compliance Trestle workspace) |
| `routing/` | tag router: profile → components → operations |
| `enforcement/` | boundary compiler: OSCAL rules → grants, budgets, OpenFlow policy |
| `consumer/` | drop-in consumer apps (team chat first) |
| `cms/` | the CMS and its control behaviours (background) |
| `web3/` | index log, Merkle anchoring |
| `ui/` | Svelte components for the 3tched.com app |
| `START-HERE.md`, `CONTEXT.md` | open in Junie; CONTEXT.md bundles every doc (rebuild with `tools/build-context.sh`) |
| `docs/` | 3tched resources, subsidiary/sled model, prior art and positioning, how to win |
| `SPARK-BRIEF.md` | current state, rules, open issues, progress log |

## Working rules

- Read `SPARK-BRIEF.md` before starting; log progress at its end (dated).
- Mark claims as **proven** (demonstrated, with evidence) or **planned**.
- Schemas here are drafts; promoted ones become sealed 3tched plugins (Rust).
- UI: Svelte/SvelteKit + json-render's Svelte renderer only.
- In pitches say "implements and evidences these controls", never
  "compliant" or "certified".

# Drop-in spec: one generator, every surface

The drop-in is the existing 3tched UI generator, repurposed: the same spec
pipeline that renders the web UI also renders into consumer apps (team chat
first), and every action it exposes is governed by the new compliance
routing, policy and enforcement.

Marked **existing** (3tched today, used through its interfaces) or **new**
(built and judged in this repository).

## 1. What the generator does today (existing)

| Capability | Where it lives |
|---|---|
| **Catalog**: the components a UI may use, as sealed declarations (Canvas profile, whole-application contract, imported shadcn component schemas) | `json_render` plugin: `list_catalog`, `list_components`, `get_component_schema`, `get_catalog_entry` |
| **Spec**: a json-render element tree, validated against the catalog | `json_render`: `get_spec_schema`, `validate_spec`, `export_json_schema` |
| **Generation**: the model is given the catalog surface and writes a spec; the spec is validated before rendering | `json_render`: `build_prompt_surface`; chat application mode (`json_render_generation`) |
| **Deterministic rendering**: a UI built directly from a plugin's sealed schema, no model involved | `schema_renderer`: `render_schema`, `get_rendering`, `validate_schema`, `list_galleries` |
| **Gallery**: specs a human kept, saved as candidates and promoted into catalog entries | `json_render`: `save_candidate`, `list_candidates`, `promote_candidate`, `retire_catalog_entry` |
| **Actions and events**: elements bound to plugin operations; events handled and components updated | `json_render`: `list_actions`; `web_ui`: `render_page`, `handle_event`, `update_component` |
| **Renderers** | `json_render`: `list_renderers`, `list_packages`; web renderer: json-render's Svelte renderer in 3tched.com |

Rules that carry over unchanged: every visible element is declared in the
catalog; specs are validated before they are shown; the plugin is the schema.

**The generator is proven** (owner, 2026-10-28): it did this job well before
any compliance layer existed. Reuse it as is. Do not rebuild generation,
validation or the catalog; the new work is only the team chat renderer target, the
five governance components (2.3), and routing every action through
compliance, policy and enforcement (2.2).

## 2. What the drop-in adds (new)

### 2.1 Renderer targets

One spec, several targets. A target renders the catalog components it
supports and degrades the rest predictably (never drops an action or a
refusal silently).

| Target | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Web (Svelte) | existing | reference renderer |
| **team chat** (Matrix message) | new — first | messages, modals, interactive buttons |
| Teams (Adaptive Cards), email (HTML) | new — later | same mapping approach |

Component → team chat mapping (initial):

| Catalog component | Matrix messages (HTML + reactions/buttons via widgets) |
|---|---|
| heading, text | `header`, `section` (mrkdwn) |
| key/value facts | `section` with `fields` |
| list, table (small) | `section` lines; large tables → attached file + summary |
| button / action | `actions` with `button` (value = action id) |
| select, input | modal with `static_select` / `plain_text_input` |
| status / progress | `context` line with state |
| **receipt** (new) | `context`: operation id, outcome, capability, event hash |
| **refusal** (new) | `section` with the exact missing capability and the rule that refused |
| **approval request** (new) | `actions` Approve / Reject, shows approvals so far (e.g. 1 of 2) |
| **redaction notice** (new) | `context`: what was redacted and which policy did it |

### 2.2 Governed actions

Every action, on every target, takes one path:

```
user action (web click / team chat button / team chat command)
  → consumer adapter (identifies the user; no authority of its own)
  → compliance router: request → OSCAL controls → candidate plugin operations
  → policy engine: allow / refuse (with reason) / needs approval (n of m)

  → result + receipt rendered back on the same target
```

- A refusal is a first-class result, rendered with the missing capability and

- Approvals are collected on the target (chat buttons) and counted by the
  policy engine; root actions need two different humans.
- Redaction is applied by policy before content reaches any target; the
  receipt records it.

### 2.3 New catalog components

`receipt`, `refusal`, `approval_request`, `redaction_notice`, `policy_decision`.
They are declared in the catalog like every other component (web and team chat
renderers both implement them).

### 2.4 Generation stays the same

# Runtime

Where things run, how to call the platform, and what the product may open.
State as of 2026-10-28; **proven** = demonstrated, **planned** = to build.

## Two roles, two users

| Role | Linux user | Where | Has |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Develop** (Junie, builds, OSCAL authoring) | `jeremy` | `/srv/git/etched-in-schema` | cargo, trestle, node/npm, python3 |
| **Run** (the governed service: router, policy, enforcement, chat adapter) | `3tched` (uid 1001) — the Hackathon subsidiary | `/home/3tched/Hackathon` | node/npm, python3; the identity mount |

Only `3tched` can act through the subsidiary's mount; `jeremy` gets
`Permission denied` (**proven**). Build as `jeremy`, run as `3tched`.

## Calling the platform (proven)

The subsidiary's operations are files under
`/home/3tched/Hackathon/3tchedfs/operations/<plugin>/<method>/call`.
Open read-write, write the JSON arguments, fsync, read the result from the same
handle. Helper:

```sh
sudo -u 3tched 3tched-callfile \
  /home/3tched/Hackathon/3tchedfs/operations/identity_sled/get_own_identity/call '{}'
```

Each result includes `required_capability`, `operation_id`, chain
`event_id`/`event_hash` and `outcome`; a refusal names the missing capability.
Schemas: `operations/<plugin>/<method>/{input,output}.schema.json`.
Live state files (`plugins/*/value.json`) currently return EIO — use operations.

The mount is supervised by runit `subsidiary-hackathon-3tchedfs` and survives
reboots (**proven**). It acts as identity `b0c777e3…`, which today also holds
**root** grants — keep demo actions to pre-tested operations until a dedicated
low-privilege identity exists (**planned**; blocked on storage repair).

## Process supervision

The host runs **runit** (not systemd). A long-running service is a runit
service directory (`run` script, `log/run` with svlogd), installed under
`/etc/sv/<name>`, enabled by a symlink in `/etc/runit/runsvdir/default`,
controlled with `sudo sv start|stop|status <name>`. Model new units on
`/etc/sv/subsidiary-hackathon-3tchedfs`. Run product services as `3tched`
(`chpst -u 3tched`).

## Network rules

- The **only** service ingress on this host is `10.0.0.2:8090`. The product
  must not open new listening ports to the outside.
- The team-chat adapter connects **outbound** to its homeserver (no inbound
  webhook). A local homeserver for the demo binds to loopback only.
- The identity container (`3tchedCtlChatbot`) has internet-only egress
  (bridge `hackbr0`, ACL `internet-only`) and no network path to 3tched; it
  reaches 3tched only through its mount (**proven**).
- Any network change must be recorded in
  `/srv/git/odbus-verified/docs/src/operations/network.md`.

## Models

- **Meta (required for the product's AI steps)**: Meta's Model API,
  `https://api.meta.ai/v1` (OpenAI-style `/chat/completions`), model
  `muse-spark-1.3` (**proven**, 2026-10-28). Credentials: `META_API_KEY`,
  `META_MODEL`, `META_MODEL_BASE_URL` — in `~/.bash_secrets` for `jeremy`
  (development) and in `/home/3tched/.config/etched/env` (owner `3tched`,
  mode 0600) for the running service. The model reasons before answering:
  give it a generous `max_tokens` (800+).
- **TypeSafe Jev** (judgments): `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` in `~/.bash_secrets` (user
  `jeremy`); see `review/jev_strategy.py` for the request format.
- 3tched's chat router (`127.0.0.1:8084`) currently uses a Qwen model; do not
  depend on it for the judged product.

## Team chat (planned)

- Matrix first; demo client Element. A homeserver is needed: a lightweight
  one (e.g. a Rust homeserver such as Conduit/conduwuit) on loopback, or an
  existing account on a public homeserver.
- Adapter: a Matrix bot (e.g. `matrix-rust-sdk`), outbound only, run as
  `3tched` under runit.

## Language choices

- Router, policy, enforcement, chat adapter: **Rust** preferred (matches
  3tched; `cargo` as `jeremy`, run the binary as `3tched`). TypeScript is
  acceptable where the UI generator's renderer code is reused.
- UI renderer for the web: Svelte + json-render (existing).
- OSCAL: `trestle` (as `jeremy`).

## Secrets

Never commit keys. Put runtime secrets in a root- or `3tched`-owned file with
mode `0600` (e.g. `/home/3tched/.config/etched/env`) and load them in the
runit `run` script.

## Logs and receipts

- Service logs: `/var/log/<service>/current` (svlogd).
- The subsidiary mount's log: `/var/log/op-dbus/subsidiary-hackathon-3tchedfs/`.
- Receipts are the evidence: keep `operation_id` and `event_hash` for every
  action the product takes, and show them to the user.

# Drop-in spec: one generator, every surface

The drop-in is the existing 3tched UI generator, repurposed: the same spec
pipeline that renders the web UI also renders into consumer apps (team chat
first), and every action it exposes is governed by the new compliance
routing, policy and enforcement.

Marked **existing** (3tched today, used through its interfaces) or **new**
(built and judged in this repository).

## 1. What the generator does today (existing)

| Capability | Where it lives |
|---|---|
| **Catalog**: the components a UI may use, as sealed declarations (Canvas profile, whole-application contract, imported shadcn component schemas) | `json_render` plugin: `list_catalog`, `list_components`, `get_component_schema`, `get_catalog_entry` |
| **Spec**: a json-render element tree, validated against the catalog | `json_render`: `get_spec_schema`, `validate_spec`, `export_json_schema` |
| **Generation**: the model is given the catalog surface and writes a spec; the spec is validated before rendering | `json_render`: `build_prompt_surface`; chat application mode (`json_render_generation`) |
| **Deterministic rendering**: a UI built directly from a plugin's sealed schema, no model involved | `schema_renderer`: `render_schema`, `get_rendering`, `validate_schema`, `list_galleries` |
| **Gallery**: specs a human kept, saved as candidates and promoted into catalog entries | `json_render`: `save_candidate`, `list_candidates`, `promote_candidate`, `retire_catalog_entry` |
| **Actions and events**: elements bound to plugin operations; events handled and components updated | `json_render`: `list_actions`; `web_ui`: `render_page`, `handle_event`, `update_component` |
| **Renderers** | `json_render`: `list_renderers`, `list_packages`; web renderer: json-render's Svelte renderer in 3tched.com |

Rules that carry over unchanged: every visible element is declared in the
catalog; specs are validated before they are shown; the plugin is the schema.

**The generator is proven** (owner, 2026-10-28): it did this job well before
any compliance layer existed. Reuse it as is. Do not rebuild generation,
validation or the catalog; the new work is only the team chat renderer target, the
five governance components (2.3), and routing every action through
compliance, policy and enforcement (2.2).

## 2. What the drop-in adds (new)

### 2.1 Renderer targets

One spec, several targets. A target renders the catalog components it
supports and degrades the rest predictably (never drops an action or a
refusal silently).

| Target | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Web (Svelte) | existing | reference renderer |
| **team chat** (Matrix message) | new — first | messages, modals, interactive buttons |
| Teams (Adaptive Cards), email (HTML) | new — later | same mapping approach |

Component → team chat mapping (initial):

| Catalog component | Matrix messages (HTML + reactions/buttons via widgets) |
|---|---|
| heading, text | `header`, `section` (mrkdwn) |
| key/value facts | `section` with `fields` |
| list, table (small) | `section` lines; large tables → attached file + summary |
| button / action | `actions` with `button` (value = action id) |
| select, input | modal with `static_select` / `plain_text_input` |
| status / progress | `context` line with state |
| **receipt** (new) | `context`: operation id, outcome, capability, event hash |
| **refusal** (new) | `section` with the exact missing capability and the rule that refused |
| **approval request** (new) | `actions` Approve / Reject, shows approvals so far (e.g. 1 of 2) |
| **redaction notice** (new) | `context`: what was redacted and which policy did it |

### 2.2 Governed actions

Every action, on every target, takes one path:

```
user action (web click / team chat button / team chat command)
  → consumer adapter (identifies the user; no authority of its own)
  → compliance router: request → OSCAL controls → candidate plugin operations
  → policy engine: allow / refuse (with reason) / needs approval (n of m)
  → enforcement: the operation runs through the identity's 3tchedFS call file;
    the bridge checks the exact capability and commits
  → result + receipt rendered back on the same target
```

- The adapter never calls plugins directly and never holds grants.
- A refusal is a first-class result, rendered with the missing capability and
  the rule.
- Approvals are collected on the target (chat buttons) and counted by the
  policy engine; root actions need two different humans.
- Redaction is applied by policy before content reaches any target; the
  receipt records it.

### 2.3 New catalog components

`receipt`, `refusal`, `approval_request`, `redaction_notice`, `policy_decision`.
They are declared in the catalog like every other component (web and team chat
renderers both implement them).

### 2.4 Generation stays the same

The model (Meta's) still writes specs from the catalog surface; the spec is
validated before rendering on any target. A target-capability filter keeps the
model to components the destination supports.

## 3. Consumer adapters (new)

| Adapter | Inbound | Outbound | Identity of the user |
|---|---|---|---|
| team chat | slash command, app mention, button, modal submit (outbound client connection to the homeserver: no public inbound URL) | Matrix message messages in thread | chat user mapped to a 3tched principal; unmapped users get read-only answers |

Adapters are thin: parse the event, look up the principal, hand the request to
the router, render the reply. All decisions happen in routing, policy and
enforcement, so every surface behaves identically.

## 4. Acceptance criteria (the working product)

1. A spec that renders on the web renders in team chat with the same actions.
2. From team chat, an allowed request runs through the identity and the thread
   shows the result and its receipt (operation id, outcome).
3. An out-of-bounds request is refused in team chat with the exact missing
   capability and the rule.
4. A root-level request shows an approval request and runs only after two
   different humans approve.
5. Content with PII posted through the drop-in is redacted before display,
   with a redaction notice and receipt.
6. The model (Meta) generates a spec from the catalog; invalid specs are
   rejected before rendering.

## 5. Out of scope

New UI frameworks (web stays Svelte + json-render), direct plugin calls from
adapters, adapters holding grants, a second policy engine per target.

and are used through their interfaces. Status as of 2026-10-28.

## The identity and its mount

- **Identity container** `3tchedCtlChatbot` — session
  `b0c777e3-0955-cd8b-3d01-ca12998cae28`, Incus pool `3tched`, profile
  `3tched-lungs`, persist volume, kept up by runit `chatbot-identity`. **Proven.**
- **3tchedFS mount** inside it at `/run/mount/3tchedfs` (and the threetched
  view at `/run/mount/threetched`), served over the lungs Unix socket
  `/run/opdbus/lungs/lungs.sock` (in-guest symlink `/run/3tched-lungs.socket`).
- Layout: `plugins/<id>/` (schema, capabilities, object metadata),
  `operations/<plugin>/<method>/{call,metadata.json,input.schema.json,output.schema.json}`,
  `capabilities/`, `relationships/`, `view.json`.

### Calling an operation (proven)

Open the method's `call` file read-write, write the plain JSON arguments,
flush (fsync), then read the result from the same handle:

```python
import os
fd = os.open("/run/mount/3tchedfs/operations/identity_sled/get_own_identity/call", os.O_RDWR)
os.write(fd, b"{}")
try: os.fsync(fd)
except OSError: pass
os.lseek(fd, 0, 0)
print(os.read(fd, 200000).decode())
```

The result carries `required_capability`, `operation_id`, chain
`event_id`/`event_hash`, `outcome`. A missing grant is refused with the exact
capability name. Live state reads (`plugins/*/value.json`) currently return
EIO — use operations.

## Plugins (sealed catalog, 72 blobs)

Most relevant to this project:

| Area | Plugins |
|---|---|
| Identity | `identity_sled`, `human_principal`, `keypair`, `users` (create/modify/delete/list Linux users), `persona` |
| Compliance & tags | `oscal_subid_registry` (register, lookup, resolve, export, list_by_category, assess_fields), `schema_tag_registry` (tags, owner-scoped policies, protected-method markers), `routing_decision` |
| Network | `openflow` (add/modify/delete flows, controller, fail mode, datapath health), `ovsdb_bridge` (bridges, ports, transact), `rovs_commands`, `rtnetlink`, `privacy_routes`, `wireguard`, `wg_opdbus` |
| Compute & storage | `incus` (create/start/stop/snapshot instances, devices), `btrfs`, `service`, `packagekit` |
| Knowledge | `qdrant`, `cozo`, `cognitive`, `memory`, `embedding_model`, `snowball` |
| Chat & models | `chat_router` (`Chat`, catalog model binding, generation jobs, config), `chat_response`, `ctl_plane_chatbot`, `model_registry`, `large_language_model` |
| Messaging | `emqx` (topics: `opdbus/wake/<owner-key>`, `opdbus/responder-wake/<key>`, `opdbus/toolsets`, `opdbus/ack/<owner-key>`) |
| UI | `json_render`, `schema_renderer`, `web_ui` |
| Workflow | `workflows`, `cron`, `elevation`, `project` |

Full list: `ls /dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs/` on the host, or `plugins/` in
the mount.

## Receipts and the chain

  written to the sled for vectorization): recovered on branch

1:# How to win this hackathon
2:
3:Ten priorities for the demo and submission. When in doubt, choose whatever
4:makes the golden path more reliable or more verifiable.
5:
6:1. **Unforgettable first 30 seconds.** The avatar speaks the exact intro
7:   script, then immediately does one real thing, with its receipt appearing on
8:   screen. Show proof before explaining anything.
9:
10:2. **Let a judge verify something themselves.** Hand them a receipt ID or
11:   on-chain anchor and a one-step way to check it (link or QR code). "Don't
12:   trust me, check it" is the thesis made physical.
13:
14:3. **Show one refusal live.** Ask the identity to do something outside its
15:   OSCAL boundary; the bridge refuses with the exact missing capability. An
16:   agent that *can't* misbehave beats one that doesn't.
17:
18:4. **Use Meta's model visibly and well.** Show Muse Spark doing the reasoning
19:   (planning the business, mapping requirements to controls), say so on
20:   screen, and let it make one real tool call through the identity's mount.
21:
22:5. **Protect the golden path above everything.** Intro → "create a CMS for this
23:   business" → provision → receipts → anchor. Run it end to end daily from
24:   Day 5. If it does not pass three times in a row, add nothing new.
25:
26:6. **Redaction is the "wow" moment.** Content with a name, email and phone
27:   number is published and masked automatically, with the receipt naming the
28:   policy. Everyone understands it instantly.
29:
30:7. **A fallback for every live dependency.** Record a full run and know the
31:   exact step at which you would switch to it. Model, chain or Wi-Fi can fail
32:   on stage; a calm switch still scores.
33:
34:8. **Tell a story with a real business.** One believable small business (e.g.
35:   a Fort Lauderdale firm that needs a compliant client portal), with a name
36:   and a problem, solved by the identity.
37:
38:9. **Say the positioning line out loud.** *"Workload identity like SPIFFE
39:   proves who is calling. Etched in Schema also proves what it was allowed to
40:   do — and what it actually did."*
41:
42:10. **Ship the evidence, not just the demo.** Public repo with a README that
43:    separates new from pre-existing work, a short video, a one-page

displayContent.text:
# How to win this hackathon

Ten priorities for the demo and submission. When in doubt, choose whatever
makes the golden path more reliable or more verifiable.

1. **Unforgettable first 30 seconds.** The avatar speaks the exact intro
   script, then immediately does one real thing, with its receipt appearing on
   screen. Show proof before explaining anything.

2. **Let a judge verify something themselves.** Hand them a receipt ID or
   on-chain anchor and a one-step way to check it (link or QR code). "Don't
   trust me, check it" is the thesis made physical.

3. **Show one refusal live.** Ask the identity to do something outside its
   OSCAL boundary; the bridge refuses with the exact missing capability. An
   agent that *can't* misbehave beats one that doesn't.

4. **Use Meta's model visibly and well.** Show Muse Spark doing the reasoning
   (planning the business, mapping requirements to controls), say so on
   screen, and let it make one real tool call through the identity's mount.

5. **Protect the golden path above everything.** Intro → "create a CMS for this
   business" → provision → receipts → anchor. Run it end to end daily from
   Day 5. If it does not pass three times in a row, add nothing new.

6. **Redaction is the "wow" moment.** Content with a name, email and phone
   number is published and masked automatically, with the receipt naming the
   policy. Everyone understands it instantly.

7. **A fallback for every live dependency.** Record a full run and know the
   exact step at which you would switch to it. Model, chain or Wi-Fi can fail
   on stage; a calm switch still scores.

8. **Tell a story with a real business.** One believable small business (e.g.
   a Fort Lauderdale firm that needs a compliant client portal), with a name
   and a problem, solved by the identity.

9. **Say the positioning line out loud.** *"Workload identity like SPIFFE
   proves who is calling. Etched in Schema also proves what it was allowed to
   do — and what it actually did."*

10. **Ship the evidence, not just the demo.** Public repo with a README that
    separates new from pre-existing work, a short video, a one-page
    architecture diagram, and a live link judges can open later.

**Bonus: freeze scope on Day 7.** After that, only polish, rehearse and fix.

# Subsidiaries and the identity sled

How an identity works as the embodiment of a subsidiary. Marked **existing**
(in 3tched today), **proven** (demonstrated 2026-10-28) or **planned**.

## Hierarchy (owner model)

- **Root**: the 3tched control plane — the only root on the system. Its chatbot is a one-off part of the
  system core, to be fused with the WireGuard server key so it can never be a
  peer (session `58287215-0136-f7c3-0a02-d51a593b75ef`). **Planned** — no
  supported re-key operation yet.
- **Root has no execution rights**: it holds authority but executes nothing
  itself; execution is delegated through the execution tracker. A human acting
  as root needs **two approvals** (two-person rule). Today `elevation` offers a
  single-use ticket (`authorize_task`, 60 s TTL); the second approval is new
  work. **Planned.**
- **Subsidiaries**: Linux users on the system. Each subsidiary is bounded by
  its home directory. **Planned.**
- **Hackathon subsidiary**: embodied by identity `b0c777e3…` (today's
  `3tchedCtlChatbot`). **Existing.**

## What the sled is (existing)

The sled is the identity. For each identity session it holds:

| Part | What it is |
|---|---|
| Record | session id, WireGuard public key, principal kind, genesis hash, trace id, schema version, active flag, timestamps |
| Instance binding | the container that embodies it (name, native UUID, pool) |
| Private leaf | the identity's writable storage, with the canonical subvolumes `@agent_soul`, `@agent_memory`, `@agent_rules`, `@agent_skills`, `@agent_user`, `@agent_shared` (shared/soul read-only; memory/rules/skills/user writable) |
| Session ledger | session events and receipts; the input for vectorization |

Session and principal ids are derived from the public key
(`op-identity::session::derive_session_id` / `derive_principal_id`, Blake3
KDF), so the key, genesis and chain *are* the identity — not a machine.

Lifecycle rules (existing): the identity subsystem owns minting; Cozo owns
assignment; login/start/stop never add or remove Btrfs members; the bridge
only verifies externally mounted storage. Never edit sled rows directly.

## How a subsidiary acts

1. The subsidiary's identity runs in its own container with a 3tchedFS mount
   (lungs). **Proven** for `b0c777e3`.
2. On the host, the same identity's mount is exposed inside the
   subsidiary's home, e.g. `/home/<user>/<Subsidiary>/3tchedfs` and
   `/home/<user>/<Subsidiary>/threetched`, bound to that session
   (`--lungs-session`) with call files owned by that Linux user only
   (call-owner UID). Other users can read schemas but cannot act. **Planned.**
3. Every call: kernel or credential identifies the identity → bridge checks the
   exact capability → MutationEngine commits → receipt. **Proven.**
4. threetched (model/agent) operations used by a subsidiary are its own:
   one router agent per subsidiary with its own model, tool set and budget
   (`max_actions_per_hour`, `max_cost_per_day_cents`). **Planned.**

## Sled + execution tracker (planned)

Every tool call is validated by the one shared execution tracker and written
to the identity's sled session ledger; that ledger is vectorized (Qdrant) so
the identity can answer questions about its own history. Code: branch
`recover/execution-tracker` (`identity_sled_dispatch::subscribe_execution_tracker`).

## Sled + Web3 (planned)

- The index's first entry for an identity records its origin (3tched origin
  session, genesis) and is anchored on-chain.
- A secp256k1 wallet is bound to the identity by a signed link recorded in
  its sled and in the index (the WireGuard key is X25519 and cannot sign
  Ethereum transactions).
- Each index entry references the receipt (`operation_id`, `event_hash`) that
  authorised it.

## Sled + OSCAL boundaries (planned)

The subsidiary's OSCAL profile compiles into: the identity's capability grants
(what it may call), router budgets (how much), and OpenFlow policy on its
network (where it may connect). The bridge already enforces grants on every
call; the new work is generating them from OSCAL.

# Tag taxonomy v1 (draft)

Tags route requests: profile → controls → plugin operations. One tag per
control in `catalogs/etched-catalog/catalog.json`, stored as OSCAL props
(`ns: https://3tched.com/ns/oscal`, `name: tag`). Mirrors live in 3tched's
`schema_tag_registry` (tag semantics + owner-scoped policies); this file is
the draft, the registry is authoritative at runtime.

| Tag | Control | Plugin operations (candidate) | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pii` | `etched-pt-1` | `schema_tag_registry/tag-registry.get-policy` (evaluate redaction policy) | redaction receipt naming policy |
| `audit` | `etched-au-1` | `identity_sled/*`, `routing_decision/*` | operation receipt (`operation_id`, `event_hash`) |
| `access-control` | `etched-ac-1` | `elevation/authorize_task`, `schema_tag_registry/*` | refusal receipt (missing capability + rule); approval record |
| `retention` | `etched-si-1` | `cron/schedule`, `workflows/*` | scheduled-operation receipt |
| `integrity` | `etched-in-1` | `identity_sled/*` (event hash) → `web3/` index → on-chain anchor | anchor record (index entry + tx) |

Qualifier tags (planned, for the router data model in `routing/DATA-MODEL.md`):
`data:private` / `data:public`, `action:read` / `action:write` /
`action:publish`, `approval:root` (two humans), `surface:team-chat` /
`surface:web`.

Rules:
- Every request carries ≥1 control tag; the router resolves tags → controls → operations.
- Tags never grant authority; grants come from the compiled profile (enforcement). A tag miss is a refusal, not a default-allow.
- New tags are added here first, then registered in `schema_tag_registry`.

arguments.content:
# Compliance router data model — proposal v1 (draft, no code yet)

Pipeline (per `docs/DROP-IN-SPEC.md` §2.2): consumer adapter → router →
policy engine → enforcement (identity 3tchedFS call file) → receipt.

## Types

```
Profile   { profile_id, catalog_ref, controls: ControlId[] }   // OSCAL profile, e.g. small-business-portal
Request   { actor, surface, action, tags: Tag[], payload_ref }  // adapter output; actor = mapped principal
Route     { request_ref, controls: ControlId[], candidates: Operation[] }  // tags → controls → operations
Operation { plugin, method, args_schema, required_capability }  // from 3tchedFS operations/<plugin>/<method>/
Decision  { route_ref, verdict: allow | refuse | needs-approval,
            missing_capability?, rule?, approvals?: {have, need} }
Outcome   { decision_ref, operation_id?, event_hash?, outcome, redaction? } // receipt fields, proven today
```

## Tag → control → operation table (initial)

| Request example | Tags | Controls | Candidate operations |
|---|---|---|---|
| publish portal article | `pii`, `action:publish` | `etched-pt-1`, `etched-au-1`, `etched-in-1` | `schema_tag_registry/tag-registry.get-policy` → redacted publish → index |
| show my receipts | `audit`, `action:read` | `etched-au-1` | `identity_sled/*`, `routing_decision/*` |
| add staff member | `access-control`, `action:write` | `etched-ac-1`, `etched-au-1` | `elevation/authorize_task` (if root: 2 approvals) |
| set 90-day expiry | `retention`, `action:write` | `etched-si-1`, `etched-au-1` | `cron/schedule`, `workflows/*` |
| anchor release | `integrity`, `approval:root` | `etched-in-1`, `etched-ac-1` | index entry → anchor (2 approvals) |
| out-of-bounds op | any | matching control | **refuse**: `{missing_capability, rule}` — first-class result |

## Decisions and rendering

- `allow` → enforcement runs the op through the identity mount; `Outcome` renders with the `receipt` component.
- `refuse` → no plugin call; renders with the `refusal` component (missing capability + rule). **Planned.**
- `needs-approval(n of m)` → renders `approval_request`; approvals collected on the same surface; root needs 2 different humans. **Planned** (single-use ticket exists today).
- Redaction applies before render; receipt records it (`redaction_notice`). **Planned.**

## Next step (code, after approval)

Rust crate `routing/` implementing `route(Request, Profile) -> Route` as a pure
function over this table + the OSCAL JSON; no I/O, no grants. Policy and
enforcement stay separate crates. Model (Muse Spark) supplies judgments
(tag suggestions); this table decides.

#!/bin/sh
# Rebuild CONTEXT.md: every project document in priority order, scope first.
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
out=CONTEXT.md
{
  echo "# CONTEXT — Etched in Schema (generated by tools/build-context.sh; do not edit)"
  echo
  for f in START-HERE.md README.md docs/DROP-IN-SPEC.md docs/RUNTIME.md SPARK-BRIEF.md docs/3TCHED-RESOURCES.md \
           docs/SUBSIDIARY-SLED.md docs/PRIOR-ART.md docs/WINNING.md review/out/findings.md \
           schema/index-entry.schema.json schema/llc-declaration.schema.json; do
    [ -f "$f" ] || continue
    echo; echo "---"; echo; echo "## FILE: \`$f\`"; echo
    case "$f" in *.json) echo '```json'; cat "$f"; echo '```' ;; *) cat "$f" ;; esac
  done
} > "$out"
echo "wrote $out ($(wc -l < "$out") lines)"

Hackathon: Meta Model API, **Startup Track — judged on a working product**.
Builder: Jeremy Hobson (3tched).

**Scope (owner, 2026-10-28):** the identity/3tched platform predates the
hackathon and is used through its interfaces. The new, judged development is
(1) compliance routing, (2) rule enforcement, (3) policy, and (4) a drop-in
consumer app (team chat first). The UI is optional. See README "Goals" for the
golden path. Sections below about the avatar, CMS demo and on-chain anchoring
are background, not the critical path.
State as of 2026-10-28. Everything marked **proven** was demonstrated on the
host that day; everything else is planned.

## The project in one paragraph

A self-contained 3tched identity — the "twin", the living embodiment of a
3tched subsidiary — turns a business goal into deployed, verified
infrastructure. It acts only through its own typed filesystem (3tchedFS),
every action is authorised against its capabilities and leaves a
tamper-evident receipt, and a Web3 index anchored on-chain lets anyone verify
who did what, under what authority, without trusting the agent or operator.
That link between on-chain artifacts and accountable, authorised actors is the
gap blocking Web3 adoption.

## Proven today

- **Identity container**: `3tchedCtlChatbot` (Incus, pool `3tched`, profile
  `3tched-lungs`), identity session `b0c777e3-0955-cd8b-3d01-ca12998cae28`,
  service principal, persist volume, kept running by runit `chatbot-identity`.
- **First-person operation call**: inside the container, write the plain JSON
  arguments to `/run/mount/3tchedfs/operations/<plugin>/<method>/call` (open
  read-write, write, fsync, read back on the same handle). Example
  `identity_sled/get_own_identity` with `{}` returned the identity, operation
  `51c8f91c-c2f1-4688-a985-fb41684adfff`, chain events 10389/10390, outcome
  completed. The bridge identifies the caller from the kernel peer over the
  lungs Unix socket, checks the exact capability, commits via MutationEngine.
- **Infrastructure operations available to the identity**: `incus/*`
  (create/start/stop/snapshot/devices), `ovsdb_bridge/*` (bridges, ports,
  transact), plus ~70 plugins. Each call is checked against the identity's
  grants.
- **No network path to 3tched**: the twin talks to 3tched only through its FUSE
  mount. Its only network will be the internet (Meta API, blockchain).
- **Chat path**: UI (`http://10.0.0.2:8080`) → door `10.0.0.2:8090` →
  `chat_router.Chat` → zeroclaw router on `127.0.0.1:8084` (protocol
  `zeroclaw.v1`) → model. Every turn receipted.
- **Avatar**: `IdentityAvatar.svelte` speaks a fixed intro script (exact
  wording, no model) and answers spoken or typed questions via the chat path.

## Where things are

| Thing | Path |
|---|---|
| Backend (Rust workspace) | `/srv/git/odbus-verified` — read its `AGENTS.md` and `HANDOFF.md` first |
| UI (SvelteKit + json-render) | `/srv/git/3tched.com` (has uncommitted WIP — do not publish it as-is) |
| UI build actually live | scratch worktree of 3tched.com HEAD + `tched_router`→`chat_router` + avatar |
| This repo | `/srv/git/etched-in-schema` — Web3 index schema, LLC declaration schema |
| Recovered execution tracker | branch `recover/execution-tracker`, worktree `/srv/git/odbus-tracker-recover` (compiles; not deployed) |
| Router config | `/var/lib/tched-router/config.toml` (root; backups `*.bak-20261028-*`) |
| Qdrant | `127.0.0.1:6333` — `repos_specs_docs_voyage_4_lite`, `repos_repomix_voyage_context_4`, `snowball_footprints`, `blockchain_footprints` |

## Rules that must not be broken

- The plugin IS the schema. Backend schemas live only in Rust plugins under
  `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/`, sealed into blobs. No standalone
  schema files in op-dbus (that is why drafts live in this repo).
- UI is Svelte/SvelteKit + Vite + json-render's Svelte renderer only. Every
  visible element is a catalog component.
- Never edit Cozo directly, never bypass a permission denial, never add or
  remove Btrfs members outside explicit identity provisioning.
- Deployment is `./activate-golden.sh` / `op-release-launch release`
  (btrfs send/receive slots). Never hand-copy binaries onto the host as a deploy.
- One Cargo process at a time; release builds need `CXXFLAGS="-include cstdint"`.
- Tests only when the owner asks.

## Plan (10 days)

1. OSCAL catalog of 3tched capabilities with a tag taxonomy; component
   definitions for 3–5 plugins (Compliance Trestle is installed: `trestle`).
2. Tag routing: profile → components → plugin operations.
3. Boundary rules compiled into capability grants and budgets (the bridge
   already enforces grants on every call).
4. "Create a CMS for this business": business declaration (start with
   `schema/llc-declaration.schema.json`) → profile → provision via the twin,
   receipts recorded as OSCAL assessment results and anchored on-chain.
5. UI: avatar intro, then "enough about me — here's what I can do for your
   business" (scripted once the business is chosen), vitals and nerve-trace
   views fed by real receipts, OSCAL views.
Golden path (must work three times in a row before any stretch goal):
scripted intro → "create a CMS for this business" from one small declaration
and one OSCAL profile → the twin provisions one or two real things through its
own mount, with a visible nerve trace and receipts → one receipt anchored
on-chain → a judge verifies it themselves.

Out of scope (owner, 2026-10-28): moving the identity between hosts
("astral projection") — no business case. Client acquisition is optional; add
it only if it fits the flow.

## Known open issues

- Meta model not yet wired into the router (no Meta API key on the host;
  Junie reaches Muse Spark through its JetBrains login). Hermes has a `Meta`
  custom provider stub (`HERMES_CUSTOM_META_API_KEY`).
- Router turn costs ~15k tokens (skills bundle removed to halve it). Qwen does
  not reliably emit text tool calls; MCP compact tools are connected
  (`https://10.0.0.2:8090/mcp`) but retrieval answers came back empty.
- Live state reads through the mount (`plugins/*/value.json`) return EIO.
- Next release will fail activation: `notebook-sources-sync` cannot pass its
  30 s check after restart. Fix before releasing.
- Re-key of the core chatbot to the WireGuard server key (session
  `58287215-0136-f7c3-0a02-d51a593b75ef`) has no supported op yet.
- UI overlay on `dashboard-release` is runtime-only; lost on reboot or release.

## CMS: compliant by construction (owner direction, 2026-10-28)

The CMS is the showcase because it comes out usable *and* evidently
controlled. Pick a handful of controls whose effect is visible on stage; each
control → a CMS behaviour → evidence (receipt or anchor):

| Control area | Visible behaviour | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| PII handling (NIST 800-53 PT) | automatic redaction on publish; original kept only in the owner's private scope | redaction operation receipt naming the triggering policy |
| Audit (AU) | every create/edit/publish attributable | receipt chain: who, capability, when |
| Access control (AC) | roles compiled into capability grants | a live denial showing the exact missing capability |
| Retention (SI-12) | scheduled expiry/archive | scheduled operation receipt |
| Integrity | published versions hash-anchored | on-chain anchor a judge can check |

Pitch wording: "implements and evidences these controls" — never "compliant"
or "certified" (an assessor declares compliance).

## Remote identities: established design (owner, 2026-10-28)

WireGuard is only the establishment step: the peer key proves the identity
once, the decoy issues the signed peer proof (OIA1) and the session gets its
sealed credential (SID1). After that it is zero trust — every call carries the
credential and the door's interceptor re-verifies it, over any transport
(internet, Cloudflare). 3tched-fs `Credential` mode is the remote form of the
lungs. The mechanism exists; it needs testing and refinement, not a rebuild.
Do not add a mesh (Netmaker/Cloudflare) as an identity layer.

## Progress log

- 2026-10-28: Junie pinned to Muse Spark for this repo — new
  `.junie/config.json` sets `model: muse-spark-1.3`, `effort: medium`
  (matches `~/.junie/settings.json` launch default, provider `meta`).
  IDE Junie routes via JetBrains login, no key needed. Headless `junie --task`
  still unauthenticated ("Cannot find authorization", proven this date):
  needs `JUNIE_META_API_KEY` from `https://ai.developer.meta.com/`
  (documented in `docs/RUNTIME.md`); same key gap blocks runtime Meta calls
  for the drop-in.
- 2026-10-28: LiteLLM wired to Meta Model API — `META_API_KEY` (48ch),
  `META_MODEL=muse-spark-1.3`, `META_MODEL_BASE_URL=https://api.meta.ai/v1`
  present in `~/.bash_secrets` and `/home/3tched/.config/etched/env` (0600).
  Venv `~/.venvs/litellm-meta` (litellm lib) proven: `openai/muse-spark-1.3`
  + api_base override returns `litellm-meta-ok` (~7s, 204 reasoning tokens).
  Helper `tools/litellm_meta.py` uses only `META_*` env, `max_tokens=800`
  default. Note: SPARK-BRIEF line 148 `JUNIE_META_API_KEY` gap is separate
  (headless Junie auth); runtime Meta calls are unblocked.
- 2026-10-28: omp in this repo is meta+jev only — new `.omp/config.yml`
  (project scope, other dirs unaffected): `disabledProviders` denies all 22
  non-meta chat providers (proven: `omp models` here lists 1 provider,
  `openai`/`salad` gone; /tmp still lists 23, smol still global salad).
  `modelRoles` pins default/smol/slow/plan/advisor to meta, judge stays
  `typesafe/jev-latest`; all `task.agentModelOverrides` mapped to meta.
  `enabledProviders` allowlist does NOT work at project scope (tested).
  Shell env fixed for consistency: `~/.bashrc` now sources
  `~/.bash_secrets` first; `~/.profile` stale `/home/admin/.bash_secrets`
  path repointed to `$HOME`. Clean-env `omp -p --model meta/muse-spark-1.3`
  returns `omp-meta-ok` (~7s). Broker cred hash == `META_API_KEY` hash.
